observation: In the initial scope broadening check, disjoint path extensions (e.g. proposal scope is src/Database but finding scope is src/Auth) were not flagged as broadened because the check only matched if the proposal scope was a prefix of the finding scope. This allowed proposals to silently extend into entirely new, unrelated directories.

evidence.summary: The test failed because ConsolidationResultValidator did not flag the disjoint scope 'src/Database' as broadened compared to the source finding scope 'src/Auth'. After applying the prefix-trailing-slash check, the validator correctly flagged it.

hypothesis: To block disjoint scopes, any proposed scope must either match the finding scope exactly, be a sub-path under a finding scope, or have the root scope ('/'). If the proposed scope starts with a finding scope but is not followed by a directory separator or doesn't match it, it represents a disjoint or broadened path.
validated_conclusion: When validating proposal scopes against source finding scopes in ConsolidationResultValidator, check if the proposed scope starts with the finding scope plus a directory separator (rtrim($fs, '/') . '/'). If a proposed scope is not covered by any finding scope, flag it as broadened, requiring a justification in the reason field of at least 15 characters.
